country: Eastern Caribbean Currency Union (Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, headquartered in Saint Kitts and Nevis)
people: Sir Errol Allen (Deputy Governor 1983 to 31 March 2005; joined the East Caribbean Currency Authority in 1974 as Manager, Research Department)
summary: The Eastern Caribbean Central Bank's own page on former governors and deputy governors sets out Sir Errol Allen's career. He joined the East Caribbean Currency Authority in 1974 as Manager of the Research Department, was appointed Deputy Governor in 1983 when the ECCB was established, and retired on 31 March 2005. The same page lists him as sitting on the Board of Directors of the Bank of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and the Board of Directors of the National Commercial Bank of Anguilla. Both are commercial banks. The central bank's page gives no dates for either directorship and does not say whether either bank is privately owned or state-owned, and the names of both institutions suggest a national or government connection that the page does not resolve. Before the currency authority he worked in the UK Government Service and with the Guyana Development Corporation. He also sits on the Turks and Caicos Islands Financial Services Commission and the Eastern Caribbean Securities Regulatory Commission, which are regulators, not firms. So the commercial-bank board seats are stated by the central bank itself, but which side is private is not characterised by this source.
source_title: Former Governors and Deputy Governors (Eastern Caribbean Central Bank)
